sample.question:
This is a Tower of Hanoi puzzle. The image shows three pegs labeled A, B and C from left to right, standing on a wooden base, with disks stacked on them. Each disk is drawn as a colored rounded bar labeled with its size number: disk 1 is the smallest disk and larger numbers mean larger disks (a wider bar is always a larger disk). The disks on a peg are stacked from bottom to top, and the top disk of a peg is the uppermost disk of its stack.
Rules:
1. Only one disk may be moved at a time, and only the top disk of a peg may be moved.
2. A disk may be placed on an empty peg or on top of a larger disk; a larger disk may never be placed on top of a smaller disk.
A move is written as "X → Y", meaning: move the top disk of peg X onto peg Y.

Starting from the state shown in the image, you want to gather all 3 disks onto peg C (a single legal tower) in as few moves as possible. Which FIRST move belongs to a shortest solution?

Options:
[1] A → C
[2] C → A
[3] A → B
[4] C → B
[5] B → C
[6] B → A
sample.analysis:
Gathering all 3 disks on peg C takes a minimum of 5 moves (found by breadth-first search over all reachable states).
Checking every possible first move (the number is the minimum moves still needed afterwards):
- A → B: 6 more move(s), 7 in total — not optimal.
- A → C: illegal move (disk 2 cannot be placed on top of disk 1) — cannot be played.
- B → A: illegal move (disk 3 cannot be placed on top of disk 2) — cannot be played.
- B → C: illegal move (disk 3 cannot be placed on top of disk 1) — cannot be played.
- C → A: 4 more move(s), 5 in total — optimal.
- C → B: 5 more move(s), 6 in total — not optimal.
Only C → A keeps a shortest (5-move) solution open.

So the answer is C → A. The option number is 2.
